references.text: The healed man tells the Jews that the one who healed him said to take up his bed and walk – a direct restatement of Jesus’ command in verse 8. [ref:Joh 5:11-12|John 5:11-12]

Jesus heals the paralyzed man and says, "Get up, pick up your mat and go home!" – nearly identical wording to the command in John 5:8, showing Jesus’ power to heal with a word. [ref:Mark 2:9-12|Mark 2:9-12]
Jesus heals the paralyzed man and commands him to get up, take his bed, and go home – a parallel healing with the same type of command. [ref:Luk 5:24-25|Luke 5:24-25]
Jesus heals the paralyzed man and says, "Get up, take your bed and go home" – Matthew’s parallel account following the same pattern of a healing command. [ref:Matt 9:6-7|Matthew 9:6-7]

Peter says to the paralyzed Aeneas, "Jesus Christ heals you. Get up and make your bed!" – a parallel command showing that the apostles continued Jesus’ healing work with similar words. [ref:Apg 9:33-34|Acts 9:33-34]
Peter heals the paralyzed man at the temple gate in Jesus’ name and commands him to get up and walk, just as Jesus commanded the sick man by the Pool of Bethesda. [ref:Apg 3:6-8|Acts 3:6-8]
The immediate result of Jesus’ command: the man was made well, picked up his bed, and walked – the command in verse 8 was instantly obeyed. [ref:Joh 5:9|John 5:9]
